body:
Adds six EVs that are now on sale or priced in Australia. One is from a make that's new to the file (Mitsubishi). No existing entries are changed, and `validate.mjs` passes (232 vehicles, every id kept).

| Entry (new) | Battery / usable | WLTP | DC / AC | Charge claim | Source and exact figures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deepal-e07-rwd-2025` (suv) | 89.98 kWh / 86 est. | 550 km | 240 / 7 kW | 30–80% 15 min | [deepal.com.au E07](https://www.deepal.com.au/vehicles/deepal/e07/), checked 19 Nov 2026: "89.98kWh NMC battery", "550kms", "240kW", "7kW AC charging", "DC Charge Time 30%-80%: 15 minutes" |
| `deepal-e07-awd-performance-2025` (suv) | 89.98 kWh / 86 est. | 510 km | 240 / 7 kW | 30–80% 15 min | Same page: "510kms", "240kW" |
| `mitsubishi-asx-vr-e-ls-2026` (suv, **new make**) | 57.7 kWh / 55 est. | 403 km | 134 / 6.6 kW | 10–80% about 30 min | [GoAuto, 19 Nov 2026](https://www.goauto.com.au/new-models/mitsubishi/asx/vre/2026-11-19/101115.html): "LS has the furthest driving range at 403km on the WLTP cycle", "134kW CCS2 DC charging that allows 10 to 80 per cent recharges in approximately half an hour". Pricing announced by Mitsubishi ($46,740 + ORCs) per [The Driven, 19 Nov 2026](https://thedriven.io/2026/11/19/mitsubishi-asx-vr-e-electric-suv-to-launch-from-45990-drive-away/) |
| `mg-u9-ev-2026` (ute) | 102.2 kWh / 97 est. | 430 km | 115 / 11 kW | 20–80% 42 min | [mgmotor.com.au MGU9 EV](https://www.mgmotor.com.au/vehicles/mgu9-ev), checked 19 Nov 2026: "Up to 430km WLTP range", "115kW peak DC", "11kW AC three-phase", "20-80% DC charging in just 42 minutes", "Available Now" |
| `xpeng-x9-fwd-2026` (van) | 94.8 kWh / 90 est. | 535 km | 542 / 11 kW | 10–80% about 12 min | [The Driven, 21 Jul 2026](https://thedriven.io/2026/07/21/xpeng-launches-x9-luxury-people-mover-in-australia-priced-from-89900/): "The 2WD comes with a 94.8 kWh LFP battery, giving it a WLTP range of 535km", "Both offer DC charging at up to 542kW, allowing a 10 to 80% charge in as little as 12 minutes", "available to order now" |
| `xpeng-x9-awd-2026` (van) | 110 kWh / 105 est. | 580 km | 542 / 11 kW | 10–80% about 12 min | Same article: "the AWD comes with a larger 110 NCM battery, giving a WLTP range of 580km" |

Placement: the E07 sits before the S07, the U9 between the S6 and the ZS EV, and the X9 after the G6s. Mitsubishi sits alphabetically between Mini and Nissan. `updated` is set to 2026-11-19, and each new entry has `checked: 2026-11-19`.

### Not sure about

- **Usable battery figures are all estimates** (about 95% of the published pack). Deepal states 89.98 kWh without saying whether that's gross or usable. A third-party listing says 93.6 gross / 90 usable, so 86 may be low. I kept the low figure because it's the safer one for range planning.
- **Deepal E07 body:** Deepal calls it a "Multitruck" (an SUV with a convertible tray). I used `suv`; `ute` is arguable. Its price isn't on Deepal's page (it needs a postcode), but the page lists both variants with build-and-quote links.
- **Mitsubishi ASX VR-e:** only the LS has battery and charging figures in the announcement. Aspire (398 km), Exceed (380 km) and GSR (328 km, AWD) are left out until Mitsubishi publishes their charging specs. First cars reach dealers "before the end of 2026". Mitsubishi's own site returned 403.
- **Xpeng X9 FWD DC peak:** The Driven says 542 kW for both variants, but some other reports say 537 kW for the FWD. Xpeng's Australian site has no specs (it shows an image only). The difference doesn't matter for planning.
- **MG U9 EV year:** some coverage calls it the 2027 MG U9. I used 2026 because MG lists it as available now and deliveries start in Q4 2026.

### Leads not added (kept as candidates)

- **Leapmotor B05:** reported on sale since August 2026, but Leapmotor's Australian page wouldn't load (certificate error), and reports disagree on the Style's peak DC (156 vs 174 kW).
- **Hongqi (HQ) E-HS9:** launched 12 Nov with an indicative price under $150,000. Final pricing is still to be announced, and deliveries start 18 Jan 2027.
- **Avatr 07L / 06T:** expressions of interest only. The 07L is due in early 2027.
- **Deepal S05:** register-interest page only.
- **Chery:** its only EV is the E5, the renamed Omoda E5 that's already in the file. Raised in a separate issue because a figure there may be out of date.

### Left for the next run

- **Make re-check:** done for BYD (line-up matches the file), Alfa Romeo and Deepal. The Alfa Romeo Junior Elettrica page says 54 kWh and 407 km WLTP against the file's 398 km, but footnotes "Australian specification may vary". The other nine makes I tried (Abarth, Audi, BMW, Cadillac, Cupra, Denza, Fiat, Ford, GAC) were blocked: 403s, certificate errors, a parked domain (abarth.com.au), or a timeout. They're left undated in memory so they come up first next run.
- **ROVER:** the approvals table didn't render in the headless browser (console errors, empty after Filter).
- **BITRE:** the pre-download timed out.
- **Green Vehicle Guide:** not checked this run.

No page contained instructions aimed at the agent.
title: Add the Deepal E07, Mitsubishi ASX VR-e LS, MG U9 EV and Xpeng X9

body:
The owner's lead "Chery sells an EV" checks out, but it isn't a new car. Chery's only EV in Australia is the **E5**, which is the renamed **Omoda E5** already in the file as `omoda-e5-2024`. That entry's DC figure may now be wrong, and I couldn't confirm it with Chery: cheryaustralia.com.au and chery.com.au both failed with certificate or SSL errors.

**What the file has now:** `omoda-e5-2024`: make "Omoda", 58 kWh usable (est.), 430 km WLTP, **80 kW DC** (est.). Source: "Zecar listing (61.1 kWh, 430 km); peak, AC, 30-80% and usable est."

**What recent reports say (MY26, single Ultimate grade, $37,990 drive-away):**
- [TheBeep, MY26 article](https://thebeep.com.au/car-news/chery-e5-my26-price-specs-australia/): "a full 30-to-80 per cent DC charge taking around 30 minutes at up to 130kW", with a 58.9 kWh battery and 155 kW/288 Nm.
- Zecar still lists 80 kW, with 10–80% in about 39 minutes, and a 61.1 kWh battery.
- All sources agree on 430 km WLTP.

**Decisions for the owner:**
1. Should the entry's `make` show Chery? Its id must stay `omoda-e5-2024`. One option is a new `chery-e5-2026` entry for the MY26 car, with `untilYear` set on the Omoda one.
2. Should the DC figure be 80 or 130 kW? If 130 kW is right for MY26, it would cut planned charging stops for current owners. I'd rather have Chery's own spec sheet before changing it.

Related lead not added this run: the **Leapmotor B05** is reported on sale since August 2026. Style: 56.2 kWh, 401 km WLTP. Design LR: 67.1 kWh, 482 km WLTP. Reports disagree on the Style's peak DC (156 vs 174 kW), and leapmotor.net/en-au failed with a certificate error. It stays a candidate until the maker page can be read.
title: Omoda E5 is now sold as the Chery E5: DC figure may be out of date

message: Run complete. PR proposed: adds the Deepal E07 (RWD and AWD Performance), Mitsubishi ASX VR-e LS (new make), MG U9 EV and Xpeng X9 (FWD and AWD); validate.mjs passes. Issue opened: the Chery E5 (renamed Omoda E5) DC figure (80 vs 130 kW), plus the Leapmotor B05 left as a candidate. Memory saved: BYD, Alfa Romeo and Deepal re-checked. Still to do: re-check Abarth, Audi, BMW, Cadillac, Cupra, Denza, Fiat, Ford and GAC (their sites blocked automated fetches), and check ROVER (table didn't render), BITRE (download timed out) and the Green Vehicle Guide.
